tagline: The beach towns' road, Michigan's first paved for visitors.
intro: From the Indiana line at New Buffalo the Pike runs north up the Lake Michigan shore through St. Joseph and Benton Harbor, South Haven, Saugatuck and Douglas, Holland, Grand Haven, Muskegon and Whitehall, past the Silver Lake dunes and Pentwater to US-10 near Ludington, 184 miles. Business loops carry it off the freeway and into the towns.

The West Michigan Pike Association, organized under that name in 1913, marked its auto trail with concrete posts eight feet tall, and MDOT calls the result the first paved road in Michigan built especially for visitors. It is often credited with starting the tourist trade that built the beach towns.

moments.title: Holland
moments.text: A Dutch-American town that bought 100,000 tulip bulbs from the Netherlands in 1928 and in 1964 brought over a whole windmill, De Zwaan, which now stands on Windmill Island.

moments.title: Grand Haven
moments.text: Two red lighthouses, of 1875 and 1905, stand on the south pier at the mouth of the Grand River, joined to the shore by a lighted catwalk.

moments.title: Silver Lake Sand Dunes
moments.text: Over 2,000 acres of dunes between Silver Lake and Lake Michigan, with a northern stretch where people drive their own off-road vehicles to the top.

sources.label: MDOT, Pure Michigan Byways Driving Guide (Wayback Machine snapshot, December 2025)
